title: Coefficient comparison for exceptional inverse image
statement:
Let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of standing schemes, $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ a listed
coefficient map, and $f^!$ the right adjoint of $Rf_!$ on $\Loc(\Dctf(-,\Lambda))$
and on $\Loc(\Dctf(-,\Lambda'))$ ([sk-thm-existence]). For $K\in\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$ let
$$
\beta_{f,K}\colon(f^!K)_{\Lambda'}\longrightarrow f^!(K_{\Lambda'})
$$
be the transpose under $Rf_!\dashv f^!$ over $\Lambda'$ of
$$
Rf_!\bigl((f^!K)_{\Lambda'}\bigr)\xrightarrow{(\gamma^!_{f,f^!K})^{-1}}(Rf_!f^!K)_{\Lambda'}\xrightarrow{(\epsilon_K)_{\Lambda'}}K_{\Lambda'}
$$
(with $\gamma^!$ the isomorphism of [det-prop-scalar-six-compact-support]). Then
$\beta_{f,K}$ is an isomorphism in $\Dctf(X,\Lambda')$, and the $\beta$ are compatible
with composition, $\beta_{gf,K}=f^!(\beta_{g,K})\circ\beta_{f,g^!K}$ under $(gf)^!=f^!g^!$,
and with restriction to open subschemes; for an open immersion, $\beta$ is the
pullback identification.

proof.text: *Definition and formal properties.* By [sk-thm-existence] (4), $f^!K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$, so the comparison $\gamma^!_{f,f^!K}$ is defined and invertible, and $(f^!K)_{\Lambda'}\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda')$ by [det-prop-scalar-six-ctf]. Thus the displayed transpose defines a morphism in $\Dctf(X,\Lambda')$. For composable $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$, [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] identifies the counit of the composite with the composite of counits; the composition compatibility of $\gamma^!$ in [det-prop-scalar-six-compact-support] then gives, by the defining transpose, $\beta_{gf,K}=f^!(\beta_{g,K})\circ\beta_{f,g^!K}$. For an open immersion $u$, [det-sf-mate-open-restriction] gives $u^!=u^*$ and [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] identifies scalar extension with pullback; hence the transpose of the scalar-extended open counit is the pullback identification, for an open $u:U\hookrightarrow X$, the composition equation applied to $fu$, with this open identification for $u$, identifies $u^*\beta_{f,K}$ with $\beta_{fu,K}$. For a target open $v:V\hookrightarrow Y$ and $u:X_V\hookrightarrow X$, the open-restriction identification is obtained from $\operatorname{Hom}(u_!C,f^!K)=\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!u_!C,K)=\operatorname{Hom}(v_!Rf_{V,!}C,K)=\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_{V,!}C,v^*K)$. Apply scalar extension to these bijections. The open-extension comparisons and the composition comparison for $\gamma^!$ identify their counit composites, so transposition identifies $u^*\beta_{f,K}$ with $\beta_{f_V,v^*K}$ as well.

*Closed supports and the chosen right adjoint.* Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ be closed and $j:V\hookrightarrow Y$ its open complement. The field $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0,k$), so $Y$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Its open subsets are quasi-compact: the finite unions of any open cover have a maximal member by the ascending-chain condition on opens. Also $Y$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Thus $Y$ is qcqs and $j$ is quasi-compact, as required below. The closed immersion is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] (a); its compactification with identity open part gives $Ri_!=i_*$. Because $K$ is bounded, apply the bounded-below condensed-ring recollement [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-open-closed-recollement] and put $H=Ri^!K$ for its ambient right adjoint. Its statement gives the distinguished triangle $i_*H\to K\to Rj_*j^*K\to i_*H[1]$ with first arrow explicitly the counit. The bounded-below restriction of the derived sections-with-support adjunction in [det-lem-formal-closed-support-derived] (1) identifies $H$ with $R\underline\Gamma_ZK$; thus this is the closed-support construction, with the normalization of its first arrow supplied by the recollement statement. By [det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images] (1),(3), $j^*K$ and $Rj_*j^*K$ are constructible of finite Tor amplitude; the fibre $i_*H$ is too, since boundedness and constructibility and finite Tor amplitude are preserved in triangles. By [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf] (2), $i_*$ is exact and $i^*i_*\simeq\mathrm{id}$ on module sheaves; these identities hold termwise on complexes, with $i^*$ exact because the coefficient sheaves are pulled back. Thus $H\simeq i^*i_*H\in\Dctf(Z,\Lambda)$ by the pullback assertion of [det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images]. For $C\in\Loc(\Dctf(Z,\Lambda))$ the two adjunctions give $\operatorname{Hom}(C,H)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(i_*C,K)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(C,i^!K)$, with $i^!$ as in [sk-thm-existence]. These natural bijections identify $H$ with $i^!K$ and identify the first arrow of the triangle with its counit. All objects used are in the full localizing subcategories, so this identification uses the restricted adjunction, not an assertion that the ambient support right adjoint preserves the entire localizing category.

source.place: Closed immersions, support identification and constructibility

proof.text: *Closed-immersion comparison, including the connecting square.* Derived tensor is exact in each variable by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], so scalar extension is exact. Apply this exact derived scalar functor to the triangle of step 2 and compare it with the triangle for $K_{\Lambda'}$. On the middle terms take $b=\mathrm{id}_{K_{\Lambda'}}$; on the third terms take $c=\gamma_{j,j^*K}$ followed by the pullback comparison. This $c$ is an isomorphism by [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image] (1) and [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] (1). Its square with the units $K\to Rj_*j^*K$ commutes by [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image] (2). Rotate the two distinguished triangles so this is their first square, apply TR3, and rotate back ([def-weil-triangulated-category]); obtain a map $a$ on their first terms making all three squares commute. Identify its source with $i_*((i^!K)_{\Lambda'})$ by [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] (2). Full faithfulness from [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf] (2) gives $a=i_*\alpha$ for a unique $\alpha:(i^!K)_{\Lambda'}\to i^!(K_{\Lambda'})$. Its first square says $\epsilon_{K_{\Lambda'}}\circ i_*\alpha=(\epsilon_K)_{\Lambda'}\circ(\gamma^!_{i,i^!K})^{-1}$: for a closed immersion the compactification has identity open part, so $\gamma^!_i$ is the closed-pushforward scalar comparison ([det-prop-scalar-six-compact-support], [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] (2)). The adjunction bijection therefore gives $\alpha=\beta_{i,K}$. Now [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] applied to $(a,b,c)$ makes $a=i_*\beta_{i,K}$ invertible; applying $i^*$ and $i^*i_*\simeq\mathrm{id}$ makes $\beta_{i,K}$ invertible. This argument constructs the connecting square by TR3, rather than inferring it from two commuting squares.

source.place: Closed immersions, comparison of localization triangles

proof.text:
*Projective-line adjunctions at each coefficient stage.* Write $P=\mathbf P^1_Y$, $q:P\to Y$, $W=P\times_YP$, with projections $p_1,p_2$ and diagonal $\Delta$. For a finite admissible ring $A$, choose $N=\ell^r$ killing $A$; $N$ is invertible on the standing schemes and $Y$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since it is finite type over the Noetherian field $k$. [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction] gives $Rq_*\dashv G_A=q^*(-)(1)[2]$ on the ordinary etale derived categories, with counit $\epsilon_K=(1_K\otimes t_A)\circ\pi^{-1}$, where $t_A$ is the projection of the Kummer decomposition. [det-ctf-finite-comparison-whole] and [det-ctf-finite-comparison-localizing] carry this adjunction to the pro-etale localizing categories, compatibly with $Rq_*$ and pullback. The tensor identification is the canonical pullback tensor isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], so the counit retains precisely this formula. For $\Lambda=E,\Qlb$, [det-prop-p1-adjunction-rational-unit-counit] and [det-prop-p1-adjunction-rational-triangle] give the diagonal unit, this same trace counit, and their triangle identities. For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ (including $\Zl$), use the class and trace of [det-prop-diagonal-tower-trace] and [det-prop-diagonal-tower-coefficients] and the proper base-change and projection isomorphisms of [sk-thm-sf-pf-adic]. Define $\eta_M$ by $M=Rp_{2*}\Delta_*M\to Rp_{2*}(p_1^*M(1)[2])\simeq q^*Rq_*M(1)[2]$, with arrow $Rp_{2*}(1_M\otimes\delta_\Lambda)$, and define $\epsilon_K=(1_K\otimes t_\Lambda)\circ\pi^{-1}$. Substitution of these formulas, followed by the projection and proper base-change identifications, gives
$$\epsilon_{Rq_*M}\,Rq_*\eta_M=Rq_*\bigl(1_M\otimes(t_{p_1}\,Rp_{1*}\delta_\Lambda)\bigr)=1_{Rq_*M},\qquad G_\Lambda\epsilon_K\,\eta_{G_\Lambda K}=1_{G_\Lambda K}\otimes(t_{p_2}\,Rp_{2*}\delta_\Lambda)=1_{G_\Lambda K}.$$
Here both inner composites are identities by the two integration identities in the cited tower statements. Thus these formulas are an adjunction over $\mathcal O_E$ as well. In each case $G_\Lambda$ preserves $\Dctf$: pullback does so by [det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images] (1), and twist by the locally free rank-one Kummer line and shift preserve boundedness, constructibility and finite Tor amplitude. Hence these adjunctions restrict to $\Dctf$. The projection $q$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]. In each case $Rq_!=Rq_*$ by the proper compactification in [sk-thm-existence], and uniqueness of the restricted right adjoint identifies $q^!$ with $G_\Lambda$ and its counit with $\epsilon$. No rational-coefficient theorem is being applied with integral coefficients.

source.place: The projective line, adjunction and normalized trace counit

proof.text: *Coefficient comparison for the projective-line trace.* For finite $A\to B$, choose one $\ell^r$ killing both rings. The Cartier coefficient compatibility [sk-lem-geo-cartier] identifies the scalar extension of the Kummer class $h_A=c_1(\mathcal O_P(1))$ with $h_B$. The unit compatibility of [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image] (2) identifies the other component of the decomposition $b_A:A_Y(1)[2]\oplus A_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_*A_P(1)[2]$ of [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction]. Hence $\gamma_q\circ(b_A)_B=b_B$, under pullback and twist identifications. Since scalar extension preserves finite direct sums and inverse isomorphisms, $t_B\circ\gamma_q=(t_A)_B$ for $t_A=\operatorname{pr}_2b_A^{-1}$; flatness of $A\to B$ is unnecessary. Over $\Zl$ and $\mathcal O_E$, the trace reductions are the finite traces by [det-prop-diagonal-tower-trace] (1) and [det-prop-diagonal-tower-coefficients] (1); the corresponding diagonal reductions follow from [det-prop-diagonal-tower-limit] (3) and the coefficient statement. For $\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_F$, both traces and classes are extensions of those over $\Zl$, so transitivity of scalar extension ([det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] (3)) identifies their extensions. For $\mathcal O_E\to E$, $E\to F$ and $E\to\Qlb$, they are the scalar extensions stated in [det-prop-diagonal-tower-coefficients] (2); transitivity gives the finite-extension compatibility too. Finally every listed $\mathcal O_E\to A$ factors as $\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^r\to A$, since $A$ is killed by a power of $\pi_E$. Use the recorded reduction compatibility for the first map and the just-proved arbitrary finite-ring compatibility for the second. This proves $t_{\Lambda'}\circ\gamma_q=(t_\Lambda)_{\Lambda'}$ for every elementary listed map, and then for composites by transitivity. In particular no assertion that tensoring by an arbitrary finite ring commutes with an unqualified inverse limit is needed.

source.place: The projective line, all listed coefficient maps including nonflat finite maps

proof.text:
*The canonical projective-line comparison.* Let $T$ denote scalar extension and $\tau_K:T(G_\Lambda K)\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{\Lambda'}(TK)$ the pullback-and-twist identification; pullback compatibility is [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] (1), and twist compatibility follows by extending the rank-one roots-of-unity line used in the preceding Kummer and tower constructions. For the counits of step 4 the trace identity of step 5 and the canonical projection maps give
$$\epsilon^{\Lambda'}_{TK}\circ Rq_*(\tau_K)\circ\gamma_{q,G_\Lambda K}=T(\epsilon^\Lambda_K).$$
To check the projection-map part of this equality, use its definition as the transpose of $q^*(K\otimes Rq_*L)\simeq q^*K\otimes q^*Rq_*L\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_L}q^*K\otimes L$. Scalar extension carries this to the same expression over $\Lambda'$: its tensor identification is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] applied to coefficient change, and its counit comparison is [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image] (2). Equality of these transposes gives the projection square; composing with $1\otimes t$ gives the displayed equation. This equation says exactly that $\tau_K$ is the transpose defining $\beta_{q,K}$, since $\gamma_q^!=\gamma_q$ for proper $q$ ([det-prop-scalar-six-compact-support]). The adjunction bijection identifies $\beta_{q,K}$ with $\tau_K$, so it is an isomorphism.

source.place: The projective line, identification of beta with the trace transpose

proof.text: *Affine space, including dimension zero.* The projection $\mathbf A^1_Y\to Y$ is $q\circ u$ with $u:\mathbf A^1_Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_Y$ open, so step 1 and step 6 give its invertible comparison. For $n=0$ the projection is the identity: its counit and compact-support comparison are identities, hence so is $\beta$. Inductively write the projection of $\mathbf A^n_Y=\mathbf A^1_{\mathbf A^{n-1}_Y}$ as its affine-line projection followed by the projection of $\mathbf A^{n-1}_Y$. The composition identity of step 1 expresses its $\beta$ as a composite of two isomorphisms (functors preserve inverses). This proves the assertion for every $n\geq0$.

*General morphisms and the affine factorization.* Step 1 and [det-sf-mate-open-restriction] (3) reduce to a finite affine open cover of $X$. If $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is affine of finite type over $k$, choose algebra generators $b_1,\ldots,b_n$; the surjection $k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\to B$, $t_a\mapsto b_a$, defines a closed immersion $\iota:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^n_k$ ([def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-closed-immersion]). The graph $\Gamma_f:X\to X\times_kY$ is the pullback of the closed diagonal $Y\to Y\times_kY$ along $(x,y)\mapsto(f(x),y)$, since $Y$ is separated ([def-weil-proper-morphism]). The map $(\iota,f)$ factors as $\Gamma_f$ followed by $\iota\times1_Y:X\times_kY\to\mathbf A^n_k\times_kY$. Both are closed immersions: on affine charts pullback of a surjection $R\to R/I$ is $R'\to R'/IR'$, and compositions of surjections are surjective. Thus the affine description of [def-weil-closed-immersion] verifies the graph argument and its composition directly. Now $f$ is this closed immersion followed by $\mathbf A^n_Y\to Y$; steps 3 and 7 and the composition identity prove its comparison invertible. Local detection finishes the proof on $X$. If $X$ is empty there are no local checks and the derived category is zero, so the assertion remains valid.
